summary: FireFront is a web dashboard that helps researchers see what NASA’s microgravity fire experiments have actually tested. A user enters a scenario (oxygen %, pressure, gravity), and FireFront ranks tests from the BASS investigation (PSI-26) by similarity, shows the operators’ original notes, and plots where the tested evidence ends. BASS-II (PSI-25) is added as an oxygen-coverage view. Across both investigations, tested oxygen tops out at 22.7%, while the challenge brief expects a Moon-base atmosphere of 30% or more, and it notes PSI currently holds no partial-gravity combustion data. FireFront is an evidence-exploration tool, not a safety calculator. The BASS cleaning log is downloadable from the app, and the BASS-II log is in the repository.
details:
WHAT IT DOES TODAY

  • Scenario presets (planned Moon base, ISS, Earth, Custom) plus manual oxygen, pressure, gravity, and material-family controls.
  • Ranks tests from BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids, PSI-26, 121 test records) with a transparent similarity score. A “How the score works” panel and a per-test breakdown show the O₂ gap, pressure gap, thresholds, and weights.
  • A coverage map (oxygen vs. pressure) showing every BASS test, the tested range, Earth air, the expected Moon-base region from the challenge brief, and the user’s scenario.
  • Plain-language warnings: extrapolation alerts when a scenario falls outside the tested range, a confidence label (down to “Insufficient”), and a reminder that lunar and Mars scenarios are microgravity analogs only.
  • A word-for-word search of the operators’ own test notes, with run number and spreadsheet row, so nothing is summarized or invented.
  • BASS-II (PSI-25, 129 tests from 6 investigators) shown as oxygen coverage. Its files record no pressure, so it is not scored and never placed on the pressure map.
  • Downloads: ranked results and the BASS cleaning log.

HOW IT WAS BUILT


Raw spreadsheets are cleaned by loader scripts that keep raw values next to cleaned ones, log every change, list rejected rows, and write to a DuckDB database only if all automated checks pass (12 checks for BASS-II). Material labels are parsed only from the words in the label: a polymer is named only when the label names it (57 BASS-II tests do not, and stay marked that way). Scoring and confidence are rule-based by design, to avoid made-up answers.

KEY FINDING
Across both investigations, tested oxygen tops out at 22.7%, while the challenge brief expects a Moon-base atmosphere of 30% or more. No partial-gravity combustion data is currently in PSI, per the brief.

LIMITATIONS

  • The score is a similarity heuristic, not a flammability model or a safety margin.
  • BASS-II has no recorded pressure, and its flow settings are free text, so it is not scored.
  • 8 BASS-II tests have odd final-oxygen readings, flagged for review, and some materials stay unresolved.

TOOLS
Python, pandas, DuckDB, Streamlit, and Altair. openpyxl was used in the data-loading scripts. AI chat assistants helped plan, write, and debug the code (Specifically Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT).

PLANNED NEXT STEPS (not part of this submission)


Data foundation

  • A data inventory for each investigation and a traceable source reference (file, sheet, row or page) for every record.
  • Real download links to NASA's PSI source files once stable addresses are confirmed.
  • BASS-II pressure, only if NASA's Summary Report states it, with the page cited.
  • Parse the free-text flow settings (fan and air displays) into comparable values, with a hand-checked sample.
  • Label test outcomes (ignited, extinguished, ambiguous) from the operators' notes, checked by hand with a reported error rate.
  • Check the flagged BASS-II final-oxygen readings against NASA's Summary Report.
  • Resolve the remaining unidentified materials using NASA documentation.

More NASA investigations

  • Solid-material flammability: Saffire I-III, plus SoFIE and FLARE as they become available in PSI.
  • Smoke detection (SAME, SAME-R, DAFT) and flame suppression (FLEX, FLEX-2).
  • ACME's high-oxygen gas-flame tests (up to 85% O₂), reported as a separate kind of evidence from solid materials.
  • Partial-gravity data once NASA adds it (for example LUCI and FM2), checked against the Moon-base presets.

Analysis

An O₂-versus-flow flammability map built from the labeled outcomes, with uncertainty shown.

Tiered material matching: exact material, same polymer family, not specified, mismatch.

The range and spread of outcomes among matching tests, not only a single score.

Confidence that accounts for sample size and condition coverage, raised above "Moderate" only when two or more investigations with pressure data agree.

A sensitivity check on the score weights and thresholds, and expert review of the thresholds.

Prevention, detection, and suppression tags on every investigation.

Investigation Explorer

  • A catalog page with objectives, approaches, measurements, materials, hardware, and publication links.
  • Side-by-side comparison only for variables that are genuinely comparable.

AI research assistant

  • Plain-language explanations of ranked results, with a validator that checks every cited run and quoted note against the retrieved rows, rejects banned wording, and falls back to the rule-based result if a check fails.
  • Cited answers drawn from NASA reports and publications through document search, with evidence-gap flags.
  • A structured Evidence Brief for each question: answer, evidence, confidence, why, and open questions.
  • An option to run with a local model or with no model, so the core tool works offline.

Earth applications

  • A panel on terrestrial fire-safety spin-offs such as water-mist extinguishers, smoke detection, and firefighter gear, with sources.
  • An "Earth mode" showing which findings transfer to normal gravity and which do not.

Quality and design

  • Automated unit tests run on every push (GitHub Actions).
  • A clearer verdict-style layout, better mobile support, and home-screen install.
  • One-click export of a scenario report (PDF) and CSV export of test conditions for modeling.
  • A Docker image for one-command local runs, with versioned dataset snapshots.
  • A README with a roadmap and a "Changes since submission" log.
